from.place: Proof paragraph 2, the three displayed derived Hom objects: generic dg-quotient infrastructure through the recorded ancestry, specifically the finite-cone argument in the final step of lem-coef-dg-quotient-hom-cone. The triangulated structure is obtained from a general cone-closed module-category criterion, before proving invariance of the finite hull. Abstract dg-category axioms (A), (B), (C) supply the generic triangulation theorem used after the module and sign checks.

title: Triangulation from the abstract dg-category axioms A, B and C
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a small cochain dg category over $\mathbf Z$ as in [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure]. Write $Z^0\mathcal A$ for its category of closed degree-zero maps and $H^0\mathcal A$ for its category of degree-zero cohomology classes. Assume (A) there is a zero object and each pair $x,z$ has a dg direct sum: an object with closed degree-zero inclusions and projections satisfying the biproduct identities. Assume (B) there are dg functors $[n]$, $n\in\mathbf Z$, with $[0]=1$, $[n+m]=[n][m]$, and isomorphisms of cochain complexes $\mathcal A(x,y[n])\cong\mathcal A(x,y)[n]$ compatible with composition, with $V[n]^j=V^{j+n}$ and $d_{V[n]}=(-1)^nd_V$.

Call a sequence $x\xrightarrow{a}y\xrightarrow{b}z$ in $Z^0\mathcal A$ admissible if there are degree-zero graded maps $\pi:y\to x$ and $s:z\to y$ with $\pi a=1$, $bs=1$, $a\pi+sb=1$, $ba=0$, and $\pi s=0$. For such a splitting, the degree-one closed map $\pi\partial s$ corresponds under (B) to a closed degree-zero map $\delta:z\to x[1]$. Assume (C) that for every $f:x\to y$ in $Z^0\mathcal A$ there is an admissible sequence $y\xrightarrow{i}c(f)\xrightarrow{p}x[1]$ whose associated boundary $x[1]\to y[1]$ is $f[1]$.

Then $H^0\mathcal A$, with the induced translations and triangles isomorphic to the admissible-sequence triangles $(x,y,z,a,b,\delta)$, is a triangulated category in the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. These distinguished triangles are precisely those isomorphic to $(x,y,c(f),f,i,-p)$ for closed degree-zero $f$, with cones as in (C).
